<strong><a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;dom"></a>[DOM interface](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-element-dom)&#58;</strong>

<a id="htmldialogelement"></a><a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;htmlelement"></a><a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;htmlconstructor"></a><a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;cereactions"></a><a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;xattr&#45;reflect"></a><a id="dom&#45;dialog&#45;open"></a><a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;dialog&#45;returnvalue"></a><a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;cereactions&#45;2"></a><a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;xattr&#45;reflectsetter"></a><a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;dialog&#45;closedby"></a><a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;cereactions&#45;3"></a><a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;dialog&#45;show"></a><a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;cereactions&#45;4"></a><a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;dialog&#45;showmodal"></a><a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;cereactions&#45;5"></a><a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;dialog&#45;close"></a><a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;cereactions&#45;6"></a><a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;dialog&#45;requestclose"></a>

``` text
[Exposed=Window]
interface HTMLDialogElement : HTMLElement {
  [HTMLConstructor] constructor();

  [CEReactions, Reflect] attribute boolean open;
  attribute DOMString returnValue;
  [CEReactions, ReflectSetter] attribute DOMString closedBy;
  [CEReactions] undefined show();
  [CEReactions] undefined showModal();
  [CEReactions] undefined close(optional DOMString returnValue);
  [CEReactions] undefined requestClose(optional DOMString returnValue);
};
```

The <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;the&#45;dialog&#45;element"></a><code>[dialog](#the-dialog-element)</code> element represents a transitory part of an application&#44; in the form of a small window &#40;&#34;dialog box&#34;&#41;&#44; which the user interacts with to perform a task or gather information&#46; Once the user is done&#44; the dialog can be automatically closed by the application&#44; or manually closed by the user&#46;

Especially for modal dialogs&#44; which are a familiar pattern across all types of applications&#44; authors should work to ensure that dialogs in their web applications behave in a way that is familiar to users of non&#45;web applications&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

As with all HTML elements&#44; it is not conforming to use the <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[dialog](#the-dialog-element)</code> element when attempting to represent another type of control&#46; For example&#44; context menus&#44; tooltips&#44; and popup listboxes are not dialog boxes&#44; so abusing the <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[dialog](#the-dialog-element)</code> element to implement these patterns is incorrect&#46;

An important part of user&#45;facing dialog behavior is the placement of initial focus&#46; The <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;dialog&#45;focusing&#45;steps"></a>[dialog focusing steps](#dialog-focusing-steps) attempt to pick a good candidate for initial focus when a dialog is shown&#44; but might not be a substitute for authors carefully thinking through the correct choice to match user expectations for a specific dialog&#46; As such&#44; authors should use the <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autofocus"></a><code>[autofocus](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#attr-fe-autofocus)</code> attribute on the descendant element of the dialog that the user is expected to immediately interact with after the dialog opens&#46; If there is no such element&#44; then authors should use the <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autofocus&#45;2"></a><code>[autofocus](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#attr-fe-autofocus)</code> attribute on the <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#45;4"></a><code>[dialog](#the-dialog-element)</code> element itself&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

In the following example&#44; a dialog is used for editing the details of a product in an inventory management web application&#46;

``` text
<dialog>
  <label>Product Number <input type="text" readonly></label>
  <label>Product Name <input type="text" autofocus></label>
</dialog>
```

If the <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autofocus&#45;3"></a><code>[autofocus](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#attr-fe-autofocus)</code> attribute was not present&#44; the Product Number field would have been focused by the dialog focusing steps&#46; Although that is reasonable behavior&#44; the author determined that the more relevant field to focus was the Product Name field&#44; as the Product Number field is readonly and expects no user input&#46; So&#44; the author used autofocus to override the default&#46;

Even if the author wants to focus the Product Number field by default&#44; they are best off explicitly specifying that by using autofocus on that <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;the&#45;input&#45;element"></a><code>[input](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#the-input-element)</code> element&#46; This makes the intent obvious to future readers of the code&#44; and ensures the code stays robust in the face of future updates&#46; &#40;For example&#44; if another developer added a close button&#44; and positioned it in the node tree before the Product Number field&#41;&#46;

Another important aspect of user behavior is whether dialogs are scrollable or not&#46; In some cases&#44; overflow &#40;and thus scrollability&#41; cannot be avoided&#44; e&#46;g&#46;&#44; when it is caused by the user&#39;s high text zoom settings&#46; But in general&#44; scrollable dialogs are not expected by users&#46; Adding large text nodes directly to dialog elements is particularly bad as this is likely to cause the dialog element itself to overflow&#46; Authors are best off avoiding them&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

The following terms of service dialog respects the above suggestions&#46;

``` text
<dialog style="height: 80vh;">
  <div style="overflow: auto; height: 60vh;" autofocus>
    <p>By placing an order via this Web site on the first day of the fourth month of the year
    2010 Anno Domini, you agree to grant Us a non-transferable option to claim, for now and for
    ever more, your immortal soul.</p>
    <p>Should We wish to exercise this option, you agree to surrender your immortal soul,
    and any claim you may have on it, within 5 (five) working days of receiving written
    notification from  this site or one of its duly authorized minions.</p>
    <!-- ... etc., with many more <p> elements ... -->
  </div>
  <form method="dialog">
    <button type="submit" value="agree">Agree</button>
    <button type="submit" value="disagree">Disagree</button>
  </form>
</dialog>
```

Note how the <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;dialog&#45;focusing&#45;steps&#45;2"></a>[dialog focusing steps](#dialog-focusing-steps) would have picked the scrollable <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;the&#45;div&#45;element"></a><code>[div](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-div-element)</code> element by default&#44; but similarly to the previous example&#44; we have placed <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autofocus&#45;4"></a><code>[autofocus](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#attr-fe-autofocus)</code> on the <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;the&#45;div&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[div](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-div-element)</code> so as to be more explicit and robust against future changes&#46;

In contrast&#44; if the <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;the&#45;p&#45;element"></a><code>[p](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-p-element)</code> elements expressing the terms of service did not have such a wrapper <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;the&#45;div&#45;element&#45;3"></a><code>[div](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-div-element)</code> element&#44; then the <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#45;5"></a><code>[dialog](#the-dialog-element)</code> itself would become scrollable&#44; violating the above advice&#46; Furthermore&#44; in the absence of any <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;autofocus&#45;5"></a><code>[autofocus](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#attr-fe-autofocus)</code> attribute&#44; such a markup pattern would have violated the above advice and tripped up the <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;dialog&#45;focusing&#45;steps&#45;3"></a>[dialog focusing steps](#dialog-focusing-steps)&#39;s default behavior&#44; and caused focus to jump to the Agree <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;the&#45;button&#45;element"></a><code>[button](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#the-button-element)</code>&#44; which is a bad user experience&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

This dialog box has some small print&#46; The <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;the&#45;strong&#45;element"></a><code>[strong](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-strong-element)</code> element is used to draw the user&#39;s attention to the more important part&#46;

``` text
<dialog>
 <h1>Add to Wallet</h1>
 <p><strong><label for=amt>How many gold coins do you want to add to your wallet?</label></strong></p>
 <p><input id=amt name=amt type=number min=0 step=0.01 value=100></p>
 <p><small>You add coins at your own risk.</small></p>
 <p><label><input name=round type=checkbox> Only add perfectly round coins</label></p>
 <p><input type=button onclick="submit()" value="Add Coins"></p>
</dialog>
```

------------------------------------------------------------------------

The <a id="attr&#45;dialog&#45;open"></a><strong><code>open</code></strong> attribute is a <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;boolean&#45;attribute"></a>[boolean attribute](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#boolean-attribute)&#46; When specified&#44; it indicates that the <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#45;6"></a><code>[dialog](#the-dialog-element)</code> element is active and that the user can interact with it&#46;

The <a id="attr&#45;dialog&#45;closedby"></a><strong><code>closedby</code></strong> content attribute is an <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;enumerated&#45;attribute"></a>[enumerated attribute](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#enumerated-attribute) with the following keywords and states&#58;

<table><thead><tr><th>Keyword      </th><th>State      </th><th>Brief description    </th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td><dfn data-dfn-for="dialog/closedby" id="attr-dialog-closedby-any" data-dfn-type="attr-value"><code>any</code></dfn>      </td><td><dfn id="attr-dialog-closedby-any-state">Any</dfn>      </td><td><a href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#close-request" id="the-dialog-element:close-request">Close requests</a> or clicks outside close the dialog&#46;     </td></tr><tr><td><dfn data-dfn-for="dialog/closedby" id="attr-dialog-closedby-closerequest" data-dfn-type="attr-value"><code>closerequest</code></dfn>      </td><td><dfn id="attr-dialog-closedby-closerequest-state">Close Request</dfn>      </td><td><a href="https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#close-request" id="the-dialog-element:close-request-2">Close requests</a> close the dialog&#46;     </td></tr><tr><td><dfn data-dfn-for="dialog/closedby" id="attr-dialog-closedby-none" data-dfn-type="attr-value"><code>none</code></dfn>      </td><td><dfn id="attr-dialog-closedby-none-state">None</dfn>      </td><td>No user actions automatically close the dialog&#46;   </td></tr></tbody></table>

The <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;dialog&#45;closedby&#45;2"></a><code>[closedby](#attr-dialog-closedby)</code> attribute&#39;s <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;invalid&#45;value&#45;default"></a><em>[invalid value default](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#invalid-value-default)</em> and <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;missing&#45;value&#45;default"></a><em>[missing value default](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#missing-value-default)</em> are both the <a id="attr&#45;dialog&#45;closedby&#45;auto&#45;state"></a><strong>Auto</strong> state&#46;

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

The <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;dialog&#45;closedby&#45;auto&#45;state"></a>[Auto](#attr-dialog-closedby-auto-state) state behaves as <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;dialog&#45;closedby&#45;closerequest&#45;state"></a>[Close Request](#attr-dialog-closedby-closerequest-state) state when the <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#45;7"></a><code>[dialog](#the-dialog-element)</code> was shown using its <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;dialog&#45;showmodal&#45;2"></a><code>[showModal&#40;&#41;](#dom-dialog-showmodal)</code> method&#59; otherwise the <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;dialog&#45;closedby&#45;none&#45;state"></a>[None](#attr-dialog-closedby-none-state) state&#46;

A <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#45;8"></a><code>[dialog](#the-dialog-element)</code> element without an <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;dialog&#45;open&#45;2"></a><code>[open](#attr-dialog-open)</code> attribute specified should not be shown to the user&#46; This requirement may be implemented indirectly through the style layer&#46; For example&#44; user agents that [support the suggested default rendering](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#renderingUA) implement this requirement using the CSS rules described in the [Rendering section](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#rendering)&#46;

<a id="note&#45;dialog&#45;remove&#45;open&#45;attribute"></a>

<strong>Note&#58;</strong>

[](#note-dialog-remove-open-attribute)

Removing the <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;dialog&#45;open&#45;3"></a><code>[open](#attr-dialog-open)</code> attribute will usually hide the dialog&#46; However&#44; doing so has a number of strange additional consequences&#58;

- The <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;event&#45;close"></a><code>[close](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#event-close)</code> event will not be fired&#46;

- The <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;dialog&#45;close&#45;2"></a><code>[close&#40;&#41;](#dom-dialog-close)</code> method&#44; and any <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;close&#45;request&#45;3"></a>[close requests](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#close-request)&#44; will no longer be able to close the dialog&#46;

- If the dialog was shown using its <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;dialog&#45;showmodal&#45;3"></a><code>[showModal&#40;&#41;](#dom-dialog-showmodal)</code> method&#44; the <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;document"></a><code>[Document](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#document)</code> will still be <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;blocked&#45;by&#45;a&#45;modal&#45;dialog"></a>[blocked](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#blocked-by-a-modal-dialog)&#46;

For these reasons&#44; it is generally better to never remove the <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;dialog&#45;open&#45;4"></a><code>[open](#attr-dialog-open)</code> attribute manually&#46; Instead&#44; use the <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;dialog&#45;requestclose&#45;2"></a><code>[requestClose&#40;&#41;](#dom-dialog-requestclose)</code> or <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;dialog&#45;close&#45;3"></a><code>[close&#40;&#41;](#dom-dialog-close)</code> methods to close the dialog&#44; or the <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;hidden"></a><code>[hidden](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#attr-hidden)</code> attribute to hide it&#46;

The <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;tabindex"></a><code>[tabindex](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#attr-tabindex)</code> attribute must not be specified on <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#45;9"></a><code>[dialog](#the-dialog-element)</code> elements&#46;

<strong><code><var>dialog</var>&#46;<a id="dom&#45;dialog&#45;showmodal&#45;dev"></a>[showModal](#dom-dialog-showmodal)&#40;&#41;</code></strong>

<strong><code><var>dialog</var>&#46;<a id="dom&#45;dialog&#45;close&#45;dev"></a>[close](#dom-dialog-close)&#40;&#91; <var>result</var> &#93;&#41;</code></strong>

Closes the <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#45;12"></a><code>[dialog](#the-dialog-element)</code> element&#46;

The argument&#44; if provided&#44; provides a return value&#46;

<strong><code><var>dialog</var>&#46;<a id="dom&#45;dialog&#45;requestclose&#45;dev"></a>[requestClose](#dom-dialog-requestclose)&#40;&#91; <var>result</var> &#93;&#41;</code></strong>

Acts as if a <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;close&#45;request&#45;4"></a>[close request](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#close-request) was sent targeting <var>dialog</var>&#44; by first firing a <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;event&#45;cancel"></a><code>[cancel](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#event-cancel)</code> event&#44; and if that event is not canceled with <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;event&#45;preventdefault"></a><code>[preventDefault&#40;&#41;](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-event-preventdefault)</code>&#44; proceeding to close the <var>dialog</var> in the same way as the <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;dom&#45;dialog&#45;close&#45;4"></a><code>[close&#40;&#41;](#dom-dialog-close)</code> method &#40;including firing a <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;event&#45;close&#45;2"></a><code>[close](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#event-close)</code> event&#41;&#46;

This is a helper utility that can be used to consolidate cancelation and closing logic into the <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;event&#45;cancel&#45;2"></a><code>[cancel](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#event-cancel)</code> and <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;event&#45;close&#45;3"></a><code>[close](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#event-close)</code> event handlers&#44; by having all non&#45;<a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;close&#45;request&#45;5"></a>[close request](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#close-request) closing affordances call this method&#46;

Note that this method ignores the <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;dialog&#45;closedby&#45;3"></a><code>[closedby](#attr-dialog-closedby)</code> attribute&#58; that is&#44; even if <a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;dialog&#45;closedby&#45;4"></a><code>[closedby](#attr-dialog-closedby)</code> is set to &#34;<a id="the&#45;dialog&#45;element&#58;attr&#45;dialog&#45;closedby&#45;none"></a><code>[none](#attr-dialog-closedby-none)</code>&#34;&#44; the same behavior will apply&#46;

The argument&#44; if provided&#44; provides a return value&#46;

<strong><code><var>dialog</var>&#46;<a id="dom&#45;dialog&#45;returnvalue&#45;dev"></a>[returnValue](#dom-dialog-returnvalue) &#91; &#61; <var>result</var> &#93;</code></strong>

<strong>✔</strong>MDN

[HTMLDialogElement&#47;returnValue](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/HTMLDialogElement/returnValue)

Support in all current engines&#46;

Firefox98&#43;Safari15&#46;4&#43;Chrome37&#43;

Opera&#63;Edge79&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge &#40;Legacy&#41;&#63;Internet ExplorerNo
