#### <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;intro"></a>4&#46;13&#46;1 Introduction[](#custom-elements-intro)

<em>This section is non&#45;normative&#46;</em>

<a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;intro&#58;custom&#45;element"></a>[Custom elements](#custom-element) provide a way for authors to build their own fully&#45;featured DOM elements&#46; Although authors could always use non&#45;standard elements in their documents&#44; with application&#45;specific behavior added after the fact by scripting or similar&#44; such elements have historically been non&#45;conforming and not very functional&#46; By <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;intro&#58;element&#45;definition"></a>[defining](#element-definition) a custom element&#44; authors can inform the parser how to properly construct an element and how elements of that class should react to changes&#46;

Custom elements are part of a larger effort to &#34;rationalise the platform&#34;&#44; by explaining existing platform features &#40;like the elements of HTML&#41; in terms of lower&#45;level author&#45;exposed extensibility points &#40;like custom element definition&#41;&#46; Although today there are many limitations on the capabilities of custom elements—both functionally and semantically—that prevent them from fully explaining the behaviors of HTML&#39;s existing elements&#44; we hope to shrink this gap over time&#46;

##### <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;autonomous&#45;example"></a>4&#46;13&#46;1&#46;1 Creating an autonomous custom element[](#custom-elements-autonomous-example)

<em>This section is non&#45;normative&#46;</em>

For the purposes of illustrating how to create an <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;autonomous&#45;example&#58;autonomous&#45;custom&#45;element"></a>[autonomous custom element](#autonomous-custom-element)&#44; let&#39;s define a custom element that encapsulates rendering a small icon for a country flag&#46; Our goal is to be able to use it like so&#58;

``` text
<flag-icon country="nl"></flag-icon>
```

To do this&#44; we first declare a class for the custom element&#44; extending <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;autonomous&#45;example&#58;htmlelement"></a><code>[HTMLElement](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#htmlelement)</code>&#58;

``` text
class FlagIcon extends HTMLElement {
  constructor() {
    super();
    this._countryCode = null;
  }

  static observedAttributes = ["country"];

  attributeChangedCallback(name, oldValue, newValue) {
    // name will always be "country" due to observedAttributes
    this._countryCode = newValue;
    this._updateRendering();
  }
  connectedCallback() {
    this._updateRendering();
  }

  get country() {
    return this._countryCode;
  }
  set country(v) {
    this.setAttribute("country", v);
  }

  _updateRendering() {
    // Left as an exercise for the reader. But, you'll probably want to
    // check this.ownerDocument.defaultView to see if we've been
    // inserted into a document with a browsing context, and avoid
    // doing any work if not.
  }
}
```

We then need to use this class to define the element&#58;

``` text
customElements.define("flag-icon", FlagIcon);
```

At this point&#44; our above code will work&#33; The parser&#44; whenever it sees the <code>flag&#45;icon</code> tag&#44; will construct a new instance of our <code>FlagIcon</code> class&#44; and tell our code about its new <code>country</code> attribute&#44; which we then use to set the element&#39;s internal state and update its rendering &#40;when appropriate&#41;&#46;

You can also create <code>flag&#45;icon</code> elements using the DOM API&#58;

``` text
const flagIcon = document.createElement("flag-icon")
flagIcon.country = "jp"
document.body.appendChild(flagIcon)
```

Finally&#44; we can also use the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;autonomous&#45;example&#58;custom&#45;element&#45;constructor"></a>[custom element constructor](#custom-element-constructor) itself&#46; That is&#44; the above code is equivalent to&#58;

``` text
const flagIcon = new FlagIcon()
flagIcon.country = "jp"
document.body.appendChild(flagIcon)
```

##### <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;face&#45;example"></a>4&#46;13&#46;1&#46;2 Creating a form&#45;associated custom element[](#custom-elements-face-example)

<em>This section is non&#45;normative&#46;</em>

Adding a static <code>formAssociated</code> property&#44; with a true value&#44; makes an <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;face&#45;example&#58;autonomous&#45;custom&#45;element"></a>[autonomous custom element](#autonomous-custom-element) a <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;face&#45;example&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;custom&#45;element"></a>[form&#45;associated custom element](#form-associated-custom-element)&#46; The <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;face&#45;example&#58;elementinternals"></a><code>[ElementInternals](#elementinternals)</code> interface helps you to implement functions and properties common to form control elements&#46;

``` text
class MyCheckbox extends HTMLElement {
  static formAssociated = true;
  static observedAttributes = ['checked'];

  constructor() {
    super();
    this._internals = this.attachInternals();
    this.addEventListener('click', this._onClick.bind(this));
  }

  get form() { return this._internals.form; }
  get name() { return this.getAttribute('name'); }
  get type() { return this.localName; }

  get checked() { return this.hasAttribute('checked'); }
  set checked(flag) { this.toggleAttribute('checked', Boolean(flag)); }

  attributeChangedCallback(name, oldValue, newValue) {
    // name will always be "checked" due to observedAttributes
    this._internals.setFormValue(this.checked ? 'on' : null);
  }

  _onClick(event) {
    this.checked = !this.checked;
  }
}
customElements.define('my-checkbox', MyCheckbox);
```

You can use the custom element <code>my&#45;checkbox</code> like a built&#45;in form&#45;associated element&#46; For example&#44; putting it in <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;face&#45;example&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element"></a><code>[form](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#the-form-element)</code> or <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;face&#45;example&#58;the&#45;label&#45;element"></a><code>[label](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#the-label-element)</code> associates the <code>my&#45;checkbox</code> element with them&#44; and submitting the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;face&#45;example&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[form](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#the-form-element)</code> will send data provided by <code>my&#45;checkbox</code> implementation&#46;

``` text
<form action="..." method="...">
  <label><my-checkbox name="agreed"></my-checkbox> I read the agreement.</label>
  <input type="submit">
</form>
```

##### <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;accessibility&#45;example"></a>4&#46;13&#46;1&#46;3 Creating a custom element with default accessible roles&#44; states&#44; and properties[](#custom-elements-accessibility-example)

<em>This section is non&#45;normative&#46;</em>

By using the appropriate properties of <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;accessibility&#45;example&#58;elementinternals"></a><code>[ElementInternals](#elementinternals)</code>&#44; your custom element can have default accessibility semantics&#46; The following code expands our form&#45;associated checkbox from the previous section to properly set its default role and checkedness&#44; as viewed by accessibility technology&#58;

``` text
class MyCheckbox extends HTMLElement {
  static formAssociated = true;
  static observedAttributes = ['checked'];

  constructor() {
    super();
    this._internals = this.attachInternals();
    this.addEventListener('click', this._onClick.bind(this));

    this._internals.role = 'checkbox';
    this._internals.ariaChecked = 'false';
  }

  get form() { return this._internals.form; }
  get name() { return this.getAttribute('name'); }
  get type() { return this.localName; }

  get checked() { return this.hasAttribute('checked'); }
  set checked(flag) { this.toggleAttribute('checked', Boolean(flag)); }

  attributeChangedCallback(name, oldValue, newValue) {
    // name will always be "checked" due to observedAttributes
    this._internals.setFormValue(this.checked ? 'on' : null);
    this._internals.ariaChecked = this.checked;
  }

  _onClick(event) {
    this.checked = !this.checked;
  }
}
customElements.define('my-checkbox', MyCheckbox);
```

Note that&#44; like for built&#45;in elements&#44; these are only defaults&#44; and can be overridden by the page author using the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;accessibility&#45;example&#58;attr&#45;aria&#45;role"></a><code>[role](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#attr-aria-role)</code> and <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;accessibility&#45;example&#58;attr&#45;aria&#45;&#42;"></a><code>[aria&#45;&#42;](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#attr-aria-*)</code> attributes&#58;

``` text
<!-- This markup is non-conforming -->
<input type="checkbox" checked role="button" aria-checked="false">
```

``` text
<!-- This markup is probably not what the custom element author intended -->
<my-checkbox role="button" checked aria-checked="false">
```

Custom element authors are encouraged to state what aspects of their accessibility semantics are strong native semantics&#44; i&#46;e&#46;&#44; should not be overridden by users of the custom element&#46; In our example&#44; the author of the <code>my&#45;checkbox</code> element would state that its <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;accessibility&#45;example&#58;role"></a>[role](https://w3c.github.io/aria/#dfn-role) and <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;accessibility&#45;example&#58;attr&#45;aria&#45;checked"></a><code>[aria&#45;checked](https://w3c.github.io/aria/#aria-checked)</code> values are strong native semantics&#44; thus discouraging code such as the above&#46;

##### <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example"></a>4&#46;13&#46;1&#46;4 Creating a customized built&#45;in element[](#custom-elements-customized-builtin-example)

<em>This section is non&#45;normative&#46;</em>

<a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;customized&#45;built&#45;in&#45;element"></a>[Customized built&#45;in elements](#customized-built-in-element) are a distinct kind of <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;custom&#45;element"></a>[custom element](#custom-element)&#44; which are defined slightly differently and used very differently compared to <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;autonomous&#45;custom&#45;element"></a>[autonomous custom elements](#autonomous-custom-element)&#46; They exist to allow reuse of behaviors from the existing elements of HTML&#44; by extending those elements with new custom functionality&#46; This is important since many of the existing behaviors of HTML elements can unfortunately not be duplicated by using purely <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;autonomous&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;2"></a>[autonomous custom elements](#autonomous-custom-element)&#46; Instead&#44; <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;customized&#45;built&#45;in&#45;element&#45;2"></a>[customized built&#45;in elements](#customized-built-in-element) allow the installation of custom construction behavior&#44; lifecycle hooks&#44; and prototype chain onto existing elements&#44; essentially &#34;mixing in&#34; these capabilities on top of the already&#45;existing element&#46;

<a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;customized&#45;built&#45;in&#45;element&#45;3"></a>[Customized built&#45;in elements](#customized-built-in-element) require a distinct syntax from <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;autonomous&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;3"></a>[autonomous custom elements](#autonomous-custom-element) because user agents and other software key off an element&#39;s local name in order to identify the element&#39;s semantics and behavior&#46; That is&#44; the concept of <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;customized&#45;built&#45;in&#45;element&#45;4"></a>[customized built&#45;in elements](#customized-built-in-element) building on top of existing behavior depends crucially on the extended elements retaining their original local name&#46;

In this example&#44; we&#39;ll be creating a <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;customized&#45;built&#45;in&#45;element&#45;5"></a>[customized built&#45;in element](#customized-built-in-element) named <code>plastic&#45;button</code>&#44; which behaves like a normal button but gets fancy animation effects added whenever you click on it&#46; We start by defining a class&#44; just like before&#44; although this time we extend <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;htmlbuttonelement"></a><code>[HTMLButtonElement](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#htmlbuttonelement)</code> instead of <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;htmlelement"></a><code>[HTMLElement](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#htmlelement)</code>&#58;

``` text
class PlasticButton extends HTMLButtonElement {
  constructor() {
    super();

    this.addEventListener("click", () => {
      // Draw some fancy animation effects!
    });
  }
}
```

When defining our custom element&#44; we have to also specify the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;dom&#45;elementdefinitionoptions&#45;extends"></a><code>[extends](#dom-elementdefinitionoptions-extends)</code> option&#58;

``` text
customElements.define("plastic-button", PlasticButton, { extends: "button" });
```

In general&#44; the name of the element being extended cannot be determined simply by looking at what element interface it extends&#44; as many elements share the same interface &#40;such as <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;the&#45;q&#45;element"></a><code>[q](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-q-element)</code> and <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;the&#45;blockquote&#45;element"></a><code>[blockquote](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-blockquote-element)</code> both sharing <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;htmlquoteelement"></a><code>[HTMLQuoteElement](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#htmlquoteelement)</code>&#41;&#46;

To construct our <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;customized&#45;built&#45;in&#45;element&#45;6"></a>[customized built&#45;in element](#customized-built-in-element) from parsed HTML source text&#44; we use the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;attr&#45;is"></a><code>[is](#attr-is)</code> attribute on a <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;the&#45;button&#45;element"></a><code>[button](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#the-button-element)</code> element&#58;

``` text
<button is="plastic-button">Click Me!</button>
```

Trying to use a <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;customized&#45;built&#45;in&#45;element&#45;7"></a>[customized built&#45;in element](#customized-built-in-element) as an <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;autonomous&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;4"></a>[autonomous custom element](#autonomous-custom-element) will <em>not</em> work&#59; that is&#44; <code>&#60;plastic&#45;button&#62;Click me&#63;&#60;&#47;plastic&#45;button&#62;</code> will simply create an <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;htmlelement&#45;2"></a><code>[HTMLElement](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#htmlelement)</code> with no special behavior&#46;

If you need to create a customized built&#45;in element programmatically&#44; you can use the following form of <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;dom&#45;document&#45;createelement"></a><code>[createElement&#40;&#41;](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-document-createelement)</code>&#58;

``` text
const plasticButton = document.createElement("button", { is: "plastic-button" });
plasticButton.textContent = "Click me!";
```

And as before&#44; the constructor will also work&#58;

``` text
const plasticButton2 = new PlasticButton();
console.log(plasticButton2.localName);  // will output "button"
console.assert(plasticButton2 instanceof PlasticButton);
console.assert(plasticButton2 instanceof HTMLButtonElement);
```

Note that when creating a customized built&#45;in element programmatically&#44; the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;attr&#45;is&#45;2"></a><code>[is](#attr-is)</code> attribute will not be present in the DOM&#44; since it was not explicitly set&#46; However&#44; [it will be added to the output when serializing](html-language-syntax-parser--877d6146487f--37a9ba51eed8.md#attr-is-during-serialization)&#58;

``` text
console.assert(!plasticButton.hasAttribute("is"));
console.log(plasticButton.outerHTML); // will output '<button is="plastic-button"></button>'
```

Regardless of how it is created&#44; all of the ways in which <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;the&#45;button&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[button](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#the-button-element)</code> is special apply to such &#34;plastic buttons&#34; as well&#58; their focus behavior&#44; ability to participate in <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;concept&#45;form&#45;submit"></a>[form submission](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#concept-form-submit)&#44; the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;disabled"></a><code>[disabled](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#attr-fe-disabled)</code> attribute&#44; and so on&#46;

<a id="customized&#45;built&#45;in&#45;element&#45;restrictions"></a><a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;customized&#45;built&#45;in&#45;element&#45;8"></a>[Customized built&#45;in elements](#customized-built-in-element) are designed to allow extension of existing HTML elements that have useful user&#45;agent supplied behavior or APIs&#46; As such&#44; they can only extend existing HTML elements defined in this specification&#44; and cannot extend legacy elements such as <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;bgsound"></a><code>[bgsound](html-language-obsolete--877d6146487f--66870e9cdabe.md#bgsound)</code>&#44; <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;blink"></a><code>[blink](html-language-obsolete--877d6146487f--66870e9cdabe.md#blink)</code>&#44; <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;isindex"></a><code>[isindex](html-language-obsolete--877d6146487f--66870e9cdabe.md#isindex)</code>&#44; <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;keygen"></a><code>[keygen](html-language-obsolete--877d6146487f--66870e9cdabe.md#keygen)</code>&#44; <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;multicol"></a><code>[multicol](html-language-obsolete--877d6146487f--66870e9cdabe.md#multicol)</code>&#44; <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;nextid"></a><code>[nextid](html-language-obsolete--877d6146487f--66870e9cdabe.md#nextid)</code>&#44; or <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;spacer"></a><code>[spacer](html-language-obsolete--877d6146487f--66870e9cdabe.md#spacer)</code> that have been defined to use <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;htmlunknownelement"></a><code>[HTMLUnknownElement](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#htmlunknownelement)</code> as their <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;element&#45;interface"></a>[element interface](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-interface)&#46;

One reason for this requirement is future&#45;compatibility&#58; if a <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;customized&#45;built&#45;in&#45;element&#45;9"></a>[customized built&#45;in element](#customized-built-in-element) was defined that extended a currently&#45;unknown element&#44; for example <code>combobox</code>&#44; this would prevent this specification from defining a <code>combobox</code> element in the future&#44; as consumers of the derived <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;customized&#45;builtin&#45;example&#58;customized&#45;built&#45;in&#45;element&#45;10"></a>[customized built&#45;in element](#customized-built-in-element) would have come to depend on their base element having no interesting user&#45;agent&#45;supplied behavior&#46;

##### <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;autonomous&#45;drawbacks"></a>4&#46;13&#46;1&#46;5 Drawbacks of autonomous custom elements[](#custom-elements-autonomous-drawbacks)

<em>This section is non&#45;normative&#46;</em>

As specified below&#44; and alluded to above&#44; simply defining and using an element called <code>taco&#45;button</code> does not mean that such elements <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;autonomous&#45;drawbacks&#58;represents"></a>[represent](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#represents) buttons&#46; That is&#44; tools such as web browsers&#44; search engines&#44; or accessibility technology will not automatically treat the resulting element as a button just based on its defined name&#46;

To convey the desired button semantics to a variety of users&#44; while still using an <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;autonomous&#45;drawbacks&#58;autonomous&#45;custom&#45;element"></a>[autonomous custom element](#autonomous-custom-element)&#44; a number of techniques would need to be employed&#58;

- The addition of the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;autonomous&#45;drawbacks&#58;attr&#45;tabindex"></a><code>[tabindex](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#attr-tabindex)</code> attribute would make the <code>taco&#45;button</code> <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;autonomous&#45;drawbacks&#58;focusable"></a>[focusable](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#focusable)&#46; Note that if the <code>taco&#45;button</code> were to become logically disabled&#44; the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;autonomous&#45;drawbacks&#58;attr&#45;tabindex&#45;2"></a><code>[tabindex](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#attr-tabindex)</code> attribute would need to be removed&#46;

- The addition of an ARIA role and various ARIA states and properties helps convey semantics to accessibility technology&#46; For example&#44; setting the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;autonomous&#45;drawbacks&#58;role"></a>[role](https://w3c.github.io/aria/#dfn-role) to &#34;<a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;autonomous&#45;drawbacks&#58;attr&#45;aria&#45;role&#45;button"></a><code>[button](https://w3c.github.io/aria/#button)</code>&#34; will convey the semantics that this is a button&#44; enabling users to successfully interact with the control using usual button&#45;like interactions in their accessibility technology&#46; Setting the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;autonomous&#45;drawbacks&#58;attr&#45;aria&#45;label"></a><code>[aria&#45;label](https://w3c.github.io/aria/#aria-label)</code> property is necessary to give the button an <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;autonomous&#45;drawbacks&#58;concept&#45;accessible&#45;name"></a>[accessible name](https://w3c.github.io/accname/#dfn-accessible-name)&#44; instead of having accessibility technology traverse its child text nodes and announce them&#46; And setting the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;autonomous&#45;drawbacks&#58;attr&#45;aria&#45;disabled"></a><code>[aria&#45;disabled](https://w3c.github.io/aria/#aria-disabled)</code> state to &#34;<code>true</code>&#34; when the button is logically disabled conveys to accessibility technology the button&#39;s disabled state&#46;

- The addition of event handlers to handle commonly&#45;expected button behaviors helps convey the semantics of the button to web browser users&#46; In this case&#44; the most relevant event handler would be one that proxies appropriate <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;autonomous&#45;drawbacks&#58;event&#45;keydown"></a><code>[keydown](https://w3c.github.io/uievents/#event-type-keydown)</code> events to become <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;autonomous&#45;drawbacks&#58;event&#45;click"></a><code>[click](https://w3c.github.io/pointerevents/#click)</code> events&#44; so that you can activate the button both with keyboard and by clicking&#46;

- In addition to any default visual styling provided for <code>taco&#45;button</code> elements&#44; the visual styling will also need to be updated to reflect changes in logical state&#44; such as becoming disabled&#59; that is&#44; whatever style sheet has rules for <code>taco&#45;button</code> will also need to have rules for <code>taco&#45;button&#91;disabled&#93;</code>&#46;

With these points in mind&#44; a full&#45;featured <code>taco&#45;button</code> that took on the responsibility of conveying button semantics &#40;including the ability to be disabled&#41; might look something like this&#58;

<a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;autonomous&#45;drawbacks&#45;example"></a>

``` text
class TacoButton extends HTMLElement {
  static observedAttributes = ["disabled"];

  constructor() {
    super();
    this._internals = this.attachInternals();
    this._internals.role = "button";

    this.addEventListener("keydown", e => {
      if (e.code === "Enter" || e.code === "Space") {
        this.dispatchEvent(new PointerEvent("click", {
          bubbles: true,
          cancelable: true
        }));
      }
    });

    this.addEventListener("click", e => {
      if (this.disabled) {
        e.preventDefault();
        e.stopImmediatePropagation();
      }
    });

    this._observer = new MutationObserver(() => {
      this._internals.ariaLabel = this.textContent;
    });
  }

  connectedCallback() {
    this.setAttribute("tabindex", "0");

    this._observer.observe(this, {
      childList: true,
      characterData: true,
      subtree: true
    });
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    this._observer.disconnect();
  }

  get disabled() {
    return this.hasAttribute("disabled");
  }
  set disabled(flag) {
    this.toggleAttribute("disabled", Boolean(flag));
  }

  attributeChangedCallback(name, oldValue, newValue) {
    // name will always be "disabled" due to observedAttributes
    if (this.disabled) {
      this.removeAttribute("tabindex");
      this._internals.ariaDisabled = "true";
    } else {
      this.setAttribute("tabindex", "0");
      this._internals.ariaDisabled = "false";
    }
  }
}
```

Even with this rather&#45;complicated element definition&#44; the element is not a pleasure to use for consumers&#58; it will be continually &#34;sprouting&#34; <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;autonomous&#45;drawbacks&#58;attr&#45;tabindex&#45;3"></a><code>[tabindex](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#attr-tabindex)</code> attributes of its own volition&#44; and its choice of <code>tabindex&#61;&#34;0&#34;</code> focusability behavior may not match the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;autonomous&#45;drawbacks&#58;the&#45;button&#45;element"></a><code>[button](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#the-button-element)</code> behavior on the current platform&#46; This is because as of now there is no way to specify default focus behavior for custom elements&#44; forcing the use of the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;autonomous&#45;drawbacks&#58;attr&#45;tabindex&#45;4"></a><code>[tabindex](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#attr-tabindex)</code> attribute to do so &#40;even though it is usually reserved for allowing the consumer to override default behavior&#41;&#46;

In contrast&#44; a simple <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;autonomous&#45;drawbacks&#58;customized&#45;built&#45;in&#45;element"></a>[customized built&#45;in element](#customized-built-in-element)&#44; as shown in the previous section&#44; would automatically inherit the semantics and behavior of the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;autonomous&#45;drawbacks&#58;the&#45;button&#45;element&#45;2"></a><code>[button](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#the-button-element)</code> element&#44; with no need to implement these behaviors manually&#46; In general&#44; for any elements with nontrivial behavior and semantics that build on top of existing elements of HTML&#44; <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;autonomous&#45;drawbacks&#58;customized&#45;built&#45;in&#45;element&#45;2"></a>[customized built&#45;in elements](#customized-built-in-element) will be easier to develop&#44; maintain&#44; and consume&#46;

##### <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;upgrades&#45;examples"></a>4&#46;13&#46;1&#46;6 Upgrading elements after their creation[](#custom-elements-upgrades-examples)

<em>This section is non&#45;normative&#46;</em>

Because <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;upgrades&#45;examples&#58;element&#45;definition"></a>[element definition](#element-definition) can occur at any time&#44; a non&#45;custom element could be <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;upgrades&#45;examples&#58;create&#45;an&#45;element"></a>[created](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-create-element)&#44; and then later become a <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;upgrades&#45;examples&#58;custom&#45;element"></a>[custom element](#custom-element) after an appropriate <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;upgrades&#45;examples&#58;custom&#45;element&#45;definition"></a>[definition](#custom-element-definition) is registered&#46; We call this process &#34;upgrading&#34; the element&#44; from a normal element into a custom element&#46;

<a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;upgrades&#45;examples&#58;upgrades"></a>[Upgrades](#upgrades) enable scenarios where it may be preferable for <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;upgrades&#45;examples&#58;custom&#45;element&#45;definition&#45;2"></a>[custom element definitions](#custom-element-definition) to be registered after relevant elements have been initially created&#44; such as by the parser&#46; They allow progressive enhancement of the content in the custom element&#46; For example&#44; in the following HTML document the element definition for <code>img&#45;viewer</code> is loaded asynchronously&#58;

``` text
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<title>Image viewer example</title>

<img-viewer filter="Kelvin">
  <img src="images/tree.jpg" alt="A beautiful tree towering over an empty savannah">
</img-viewer>

<script src="js/elements/img-viewer.js" async></script>
```

The definition for the <code>img&#45;viewer</code> element here is loaded using a <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;upgrades&#45;examples&#58;the&#45;script&#45;element"></a><code>[script](#the-script-element)</code> element marked with the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;upgrades&#45;examples&#58;attr&#45;script&#45;async"></a><code>[async](#attr-script-async)</code> attribute&#44; placed after the <code>&#60;img&#45;viewer&#62;</code> tag in the markup&#46; While the script is loading&#44; the <code>img&#45;viewer</code> element will be treated as an undefined element&#44; similar to a <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;upgrades&#45;examples&#58;the&#45;span&#45;element"></a><code>[span](html-language-elements-text-links--877d6146487f--8833a85fd242.md#the-span-element)</code>&#46; Once the script loads&#44; it will define the <code>img&#45;viewer</code> element&#44; and the existing <code>img&#45;viewer</code> element on the page will be upgraded&#44; applying the custom element&#39;s definition &#40;which presumably includes applying an image filter identified by the string &#34;Kelvin&#34;&#44; enhancing the image&#39;s visual appearance&#41;&#46;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Note that <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;upgrades&#45;examples&#58;upgrades&#45;2"></a>[upgrades](#upgrades) only apply to elements in the document tree&#46; &#40;Formally&#44; elements that are <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;upgrades&#45;examples&#58;connected"></a>[connected](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#connected)&#46;&#41; An element that is not inserted into a document will stay un&#45;upgraded&#46; An example illustrates this point&#58;

``` text
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<title>Upgrade edge-cases example</title>

<example-element></example-element>

<script>
  "use strict";

  const inDocument = document.querySelector("example-element");
  const outOfDocument = document.createElement("example-element");

  // Before the element definition, both are HTMLElement:
  console.assert(inDocument instanceof HTMLElement);
  console.assert(outOfDocument instanceof HTMLElement);

  class ExampleElement extends HTMLElement {}
  customElements.define("example-element", ExampleElement);

  // After element definition, the in-document element was upgraded:
  console.assert(inDocument instanceof ExampleElement);
  console.assert(!(outOfDocument instanceof ExampleElement));

  document.body.appendChild(outOfDocument);

  // Now that we've moved the element into the document, it too was upgraded:
  console.assert(outOfDocument instanceof ExampleElement);
</script>
```

##### <a id="scoped&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;registries"></a>4&#46;13&#46;1&#46;7 Scoped custom element registries[](#scoped-custom-element-registries)

To allow multiple libraries to co&#45;exist without explicit coordination&#44; <a id="scoped&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;registries&#58;customelementregistry"></a><code>[CustomElementRegistry](#customelementregistry)</code> can be used in a scoped fashion as well&#46;

``` text
const scoped = new CustomElementRegistry();
scoped.define("example-element", ExampleElement);

const element = document.createElement("example-element", { customElementRegistry: scoped });
```

A node with an associated scoped <a id="scoped&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;registries&#58;customelementregistry&#45;2"></a><code>[CustomElementRegistry](#customelementregistry)</code> will use that registry for all its operations&#44; such as when invoking <a id="scoped&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;registries&#58;dom&#45;element&#45;sethtmlunsafe"></a><code>[setHTMLUnsafe&#40;&#41;](html-language-dom-parsing--877d6146487f--c076ab7a56b9.md#dom-element-sethtmlunsafe)</code>&#46;

##### <a id="exposing&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;states"></a>4&#46;13&#46;1&#46;8 Exposing custom element states[](#exposing-custom-element-states)

Built&#45;in elements provided by user agents have certain states that can change over time depending on user interaction and other factors&#44; and are exposed to web authors through <a id="exposing&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;states&#58;pseudo&#45;class"></a>[pseudo&#45;classes](https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#pseudo-class)&#46; For example&#44; some form controls have the &#34;invalid&#34; state&#44; which is exposed through the <a id="exposing&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;states&#58;selector&#45;invalid"></a><code>[&#58;invalid](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#selector-invalid)</code> <a id="exposing&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;states&#58;pseudo&#45;class&#45;2"></a>[pseudo&#45;class](https://drafts.csswg.org/selectors/#pseudo-class)&#46;

Like built&#45;in elements&#44; <a id="exposing&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;states&#58;custom&#45;element"></a>[custom elements](#custom-element) can have various states to be in too&#44; and <a id="exposing&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;states&#58;custom&#45;element&#45;2"></a>[custom element](#custom-element) authors want to expose these states in a similar fashion as the built&#45;in elements&#46;

This is done via the <a id="exposing&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;states&#58;selector&#45;custom"></a><code>[&#58;state&#40;&#41;](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#selector-custom)</code> pseudo&#45;class&#46; A custom element author can use the <a id="exposing&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;states&#58;dom&#45;elementinternals&#45;states"></a><code>[states](#dom-elementinternals-states)</code> property of <a id="exposing&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;states&#58;elementinternals"></a><code>[ElementInternals](#elementinternals)</code> to add and remove such custom states&#44; which are then exposed as arguments to the <a id="exposing&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;states&#58;selector&#45;custom&#45;2"></a><code>[&#58;state&#40;&#41;](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#selector-custom)</code> pseudo&#45;class&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

The following shows how <a id="exposing&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;states&#58;selector&#45;custom&#45;3"></a><code>[&#58;state&#40;&#41;](html-language-host-facts--877d6146487f--2dd822df9d5e.md#selector-custom)</code> can be used to style a custom checkbox element&#46; Assume that <code>LabeledCheckbox</code> doesn&#39;t expose its &#34;checked&#34; state via a content attribute&#46;

``` text
<script>
class LabeledCheckbox extends HTMLElement {
  constructor() {
    super();
    this._internals = this.attachInternals();
    this.addEventListener('click', this._onClick.bind(this));

    const shadowRoot = this.attachShadow({mode: 'closed'});
    shadowRoot.innerHTML =
      `<style>
       :host::before {
         content: '[ ]';
         white-space: pre;
         font-family: monospace;
       }
       :host(:state(checked))::before { content: '[x]' }
       </style>
       <slot>Label</slot>`;
  }

  get checked() { return this._internals.states.has('checked'); }

  set checked(flag) {
    if (flag)
      this._internals.states.add('checked');
    else
      this._internals.states.delete('checked');
  }

  _onClick(event) {
    this.checked = !this.checked;
  }
}

customElements.define('labeled-checkbox', LabeledCheckbox);
</script>

<style>
labeled-checkbox { border: dashed red; }
labeled-checkbox:state(checked) { border: solid; }
</style>

<labeled-checkbox>You need to check this</labeled-checkbox>
```

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

Custom pseudo&#45;classes can even target shadow parts&#46; An extension of the above example shows this&#58;

``` text
<script>
class QuestionBox extends HTMLElement {
  constructor() {
    super();
    const shadowRoot = this.attachShadow({mode: 'closed'});
    shadowRoot.innerHTML =
      `<div><slot>Question</slot></div>
       <labeled-checkbox part='checkbox'>Yes</labeled-checkbox>`;
  }
}
customElements.define('question-box', QuestionBox);
</script>

<style>
question-box::part(checkbox) { color: red; }
question-box::part(checkbox):state(checked) { color: green; }
</style>

<question-box>Continue?</question-box>
```

#### <a id="custom&#45;element&#45;conformance"></a>4&#46;13&#46;2 Requirements for custom element constructors and reactions[](#custom-element-conformance)

When authoring <a id="custom&#45;element&#45;conformance&#58;custom&#45;element&#45;constructor"></a>[custom element constructors](#custom-element-constructor)&#44; authors are bound by the following conformance requirements&#58;

- A parameter&#45;less call to <code>super&#40;&#41;</code> must be the first statement in the constructor body&#44; to establish the correct prototype chain and <strong>this</strong> value before any further code is run&#46;

- A <code>return</code> statement must not appear anywhere inside the constructor body&#44; unless it is a simple early&#45;return &#40;<code>return</code> or <code>return this</code>&#41;&#46;

- The constructor must not use the <a id="custom&#45;element&#45;conformance&#58;dom&#45;document&#45;write"></a><code>[document&#46;write&#40;&#41;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#dom-document-write)</code> or <a id="custom&#45;element&#45;conformance&#58;dom&#45;document&#45;open"></a><code>[document&#46;open&#40;&#41;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#dom-document-open)</code> methods&#46;

- The element&#39;s attributes and children must not be inspected&#44; as in the non&#45;<a id="custom&#45;element&#45;conformance&#58;upgrades"></a>[upgrade](#upgrades) case none will be present&#44; and relying on upgrades makes the element less usable&#46;

- The element must not gain any attributes or children&#44; as this violates the expectations of consumers who use the <a id="custom&#45;element&#45;conformance&#58;dom&#45;document&#45;createelement"></a><code>[createElement](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-document-createelement)</code> or <a id="custom&#45;element&#45;conformance&#58;dom&#45;document&#45;createelementns"></a><code>[createElementNS](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-document-createelementns)</code> methods&#46;

- In general&#44; work should be deferred to <code>connectedCallback</code> as much as possible—especially work involving fetching resources or rendering&#46; However&#44; note that <code>connectedCallback</code> can be called more than once&#44; so any initialization work that is truly one&#45;time will need a guard to prevent it from running twice&#46;

- In general&#44; the constructor should be used to set up initial state and default values&#44; and to set up event listeners and possibly a <a id="custom&#45;element&#45;conformance&#58;shadow&#45;root"></a>[shadow root](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-shadow-root)&#46;

Several of these requirements are checked during <a id="custom&#45;element&#45;conformance&#58;create&#45;an&#45;element"></a>[element creation](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-create-element)&#44; either directly or indirectly&#44; and failing to follow them will result in a custom element that cannot be instantiated by the parser or DOM APIs&#46; This is true even if the work is done inside a constructor&#45;initiated <a id="custom&#45;element&#45;conformance&#58;microtask"></a>[microtask](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#microtask)&#44; as a <a id="custom&#45;element&#45;conformance&#58;perform&#45;a&#45;microtask&#45;checkpoint"></a>[microtask checkpoint](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#perform-a-microtask-checkpoint) can occur immediately after construction&#46;

When authoring <a id="custom&#45;element&#45;conformance&#58;concept&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;reaction"></a>[custom element reactions](#concept-custom-element-reaction)&#44; authors should avoid manipulating the node tree as this can lead to unexpected results&#46;

<strong>Example&#58;</strong>

An element&#39;s <code>connectedCallback</code> can be queued before the element is disconnected&#44; but as the callback queue is still processed&#44; it results in a <code>connectedCallback</code> for an element that is no longer connected&#58;

``` text
class CParent extends HTMLElement {
  connectedCallback() {
    this.firstChild.remove();
  }
}
customElements.define("c-parent", CParent);

class CChild extends HTMLElement {
  connectedCallback() {
    console.log("CChild connectedCallback: isConnected =", this.isConnected);
  }
}
customElements.define("c-child", CChild);

const parent = new CParent(),
      child = new CChild();
parent.append(child);
document.body.append(parent);

// Logs:
// CChild connectedCallback: isConnected = false
```

##### <a id="preserving&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;state&#45;when&#45;moved"></a>4&#46;13&#46;2&#46;1 Preserving custom element state when moved[](#preserving-custom-element-state-when-moved)

<em>This section is non&#45;normative&#46;</em>

When manipulating the DOM tree&#44; an element can be <a id="preserving&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;state&#45;when&#45;moved&#58;concept&#45;node&#45;move&#45;ext"></a>[moved](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-move-ext) in the tree while connected&#46; This applies to custom elements as well&#46; By default&#44; the &#34;<code>disconnectedCallback</code>&#34; and &#34;<code>connectedCallback</code>&#34; would be called on the element&#44; one after the other&#46; This is done to maintain compatibility with existing custom elements that predate the <a id="preserving&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;state&#45;when&#45;moved&#58;dom&#45;parentnode&#45;movebefore"></a><code>[moveBefore&#40;&#41;](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-parentnode-movebefore)</code> method&#46; This means that by default&#44; custom elements reset their state as if they were removed and re&#45;inserted&#46; In the example [above](#custom-elements-autonomous-drawbacks-example)&#44; the impact would be that the observer would be disconnected and re&#45;connected&#44; and the tab index would be reset&#46;

To opt in to a state&#45;preserving behavior while <a id="preserving&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;state&#45;when&#45;moved&#58;concept&#45;node&#45;move&#45;ext&#45;2"></a>[moving](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-node-move-ext)&#44; the author can implement a &#34;<code>connectedMoveCallback</code>&#34;&#46; The existence of this callback&#44; even if empty&#44; would supersede the default behavior of calling &#34;<code>disconnectedCallback</code>&#34; and &#34;<code>connectedCallback</code>&#34;&#46; &#34;<code>connectedMoveCallback</code>&#34; can also be an appropriate place to execute logic that depends on the element&#39;s ancestors&#46; For example&#58;

``` text
class TacoButton extends HTMLElement {
  static observedAttributes = ["disabled"];

  constructor() {
    super();
    this._internals = this.attachInternals();
    this._internals.role = "button";

    this._observer = new MutationObserver(() => {
      this._internals.ariaLabel = this.textContent;
    });
  }

  _notifyMain() {
    if (this.parentElement.tagName === "MAIN") {
      // Execute logic that depends on ancestors.
    }
  }

  connectedCallback() {
    this.setAttribute("tabindex", "0");

    this._observer.observe(this, {
      childList: true,
      characterData: true,
      subtree: true
    });

    this._notifyMain();
  }

  disconnectedCallback() {
    this._observer.disconnect();
  }

  // Implementing this function would avoid resetting the tab index or re-registering the
  // mutation observer when this element is moved inside the DOM without being disconnected.
  connectedMoveCallback() {
    // The parent can change during a state-preserving move.
    this._notifyMain();
  }
}
```

#### <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts"></a>4&#46;13&#46;3 Core concepts[](#custom-elements-core-concepts)

A <a id="custom&#45;element"></a><strong>custom element</strong> is an element that is <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;custom"></a>[custom](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-custom)&#46; Informally&#44; this means that its constructor and prototype are defined by the author&#44; instead of by the user agent&#46; This author&#45;supplied constructor function is called the <a id="custom&#45;element&#45;constructor"></a><strong>custom element constructor</strong>&#46;

Two distinct types of <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;custom&#45;element"></a>[custom elements](#custom-element) can be defined&#58;

MDN

[Global&#95;attributes&#47;is](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Global_attributes/is)

Firefox63&#43;SafariNoChrome67&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Opera&#63;Edge79&#43;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge &#40;Legacy&#41;&#63;Internet ExplorerNo

------------------------------------------------------------------------

Firefox Android&#63;Safari iOS&#63;Chrome Android&#63;WebView Android&#63;Samsung Internet&#63;Opera Android&#63;

- An <a id="autonomous&#45;custom&#45;element"></a><strong>autonomous custom element</strong>&#44; which is defined with no <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;dom&#45;elementdefinitionoptions&#45;extends"></a><code>[extends](#dom-elementdefinitionoptions-extends)</code> option&#46; These types of custom elements have a local name equal to their <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;concept&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;definition&#45;name"></a>[defined name](#concept-custom-element-definition-name)&#46;

- A <a id="customized&#45;built&#45;in&#45;element"></a><strong>customized built&#45;in element</strong>&#44; which is defined with an <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;dom&#45;elementdefinitionoptions&#45;extends&#45;2"></a><code>[extends](#dom-elementdefinitionoptions-extends)</code> option&#46; These types of custom elements have a local name equal to the value passed in their <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;dom&#45;elementdefinitionoptions&#45;extends&#45;3"></a><code>[extends](#dom-elementdefinitionoptions-extends)</code> option&#44; and their <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;concept&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;definition&#45;name&#45;2"></a>[defined name](#concept-custom-element-definition-name) is used as the value of the <a id="attr&#45;is"></a><strong><code>is</code></strong> attribute&#44; which therefore must be a <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;valid&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;name"></a>[valid custom element name](#valid-custom-element-name)&#46;

After a <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;custom&#45;element&#45;2"></a>[custom element](#custom-element) is <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;create&#45;an&#45;element"></a>[created](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-create-element)&#44; changing the value of the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;attr&#45;is"></a><code>[is](#attr-is)</code> attribute does not change the element&#39;s behavior&#44; as it is saved on the element as its <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;is&#45;value"></a>[<code>is</code> value](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-element-is-value)&#46;

<a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;autonomous&#45;custom&#45;element"></a>[Autonomous custom elements](#autonomous-custom-element) have the following element definition&#58;

<strong><a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;categories"></a>[Categories](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-element-categories)&#58;</strong>

<a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;flow&#45;content&#45;2"></a>[Flow content](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#flow-content-2)&#46;

<a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;phrasing&#45;content&#45;2"></a>[Phrasing content](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#phrasing-content-2)&#46;

<a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;palpable&#45;content&#45;2"></a>[Palpable content](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#palpable-content-2)&#46;

For <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;custom&#45;element"></a>[form&#45;associated custom elements](#form-associated-custom-element)&#58; <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;category&#45;listed"></a>[Listed](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#category-listed)&#44; <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;category&#45;label"></a>[labelable](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#category-label)&#44; <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;category&#45;submit"></a>[submittable](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#category-submit)&#44; and <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;category&#45;reset"></a>[resettable](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#category-reset) <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;element"></a>[form&#45;associated element](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#form-associated-element)&#46;

<strong><a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;contexts"></a>[Contexts in which this element can be used](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-element-contexts)&#58;</strong>

Where <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;phrasing&#45;content&#45;2&#45;2"></a>[phrasing content](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#phrasing-content-2) is expected&#46;

<strong><a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;content&#45;model"></a>[Content model](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-element-content-model)&#58;</strong>

<a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;transparent"></a>[Transparent](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#transparent)&#46;

<strong><a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;attributes"></a>[Content attributes](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-element-attributes)&#58;</strong>

<a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;global&#45;attributes"></a>[Global attributes](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#global-attributes)&#44; except the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;attr&#45;is&#45;2"></a><code>[is](#attr-is)</code> attribute

<a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;attr&#45;fae&#45;form"></a><code>[form](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#attr-fae-form)</code>&#44; for <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;2"></a>[form&#45;associated custom elements](#form-associated-custom-element) — Associates the element with a <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;the&#45;form&#45;element"></a><code>[form](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#the-form-element)</code> element

<a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;disabled"></a><code>[disabled](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#attr-fe-disabled)</code>&#44; for <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;3"></a>[form&#45;associated custom elements](#form-associated-custom-element) — Whether the form control is disabled

<a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;attr&#45;face&#45;readonly"></a><code>[readonly](#attr-face-readonly)</code>&#44; for <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;4"></a>[form&#45;associated custom elements](#form-associated-custom-element) — Affects <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;dom&#45;elementinternals&#45;willvalidate"></a><code>[willValidate](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#dom-elementinternals-willvalidate)</code>&#44; plus any behavior added by the custom element author

<a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;name"></a><code>[name](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#attr-fe-name)</code>&#44; for <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;5"></a>[form&#45;associated custom elements](#form-associated-custom-element) — Name of the element to use for <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;form&#45;submission&#45;2"></a>[form submission](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#form-submission-2) and in the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;dom&#45;form&#45;elements"></a><code>[form&#46;elements](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#dom-form-elements)</code> API

Any other attribute that has no namespace &#40;see prose&#41;&#46;

<strong><a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;accessibility&#45;considerations"></a>[Accessibility considerations](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-element-accessibility-considerations)&#58;</strong>

For <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;6"></a>[form&#45;associated custom elements](#form-associated-custom-element)&#58; [for authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-form-associated-custom-element)&#59; [for implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-form-associated-custom-element)&#46;

Otherwise&#58; [for authors](https://w3c.github.io/html-aria/#el-autonomous-custom-element)&#59; [for implementers](https://w3c.github.io/html-aam/#el-autonomous-custom-element)&#46;

<strong><a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;sanitization"></a>[Sanitization](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-element-sanitization)&#58;</strong>

<a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;sanitizer&#45;uncategorized"></a>[Uncategorized](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#sanitizer-uncategorized)&#46;

<strong><a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;concept&#45;element&#45;dom"></a>[DOM interface](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#concept-element-dom)&#58;</strong>

Supplied by the element&#39;s author &#40;inherits from <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;htmlelement"></a><code>[HTMLElement](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#htmlelement)</code>&#41;

An <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;autonomous&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;2"></a>[autonomous custom element](#autonomous-custom-element) does not have any special meaning&#58; it <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;represents"></a>[represents](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#represents) its children&#46; A <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;customized&#45;built&#45;in&#45;element"></a>[customized built&#45;in element](#customized-built-in-element) inherits the semantics of the element that it extends&#46;

Any namespace&#45;less attribute that is relevant to the element&#39;s functioning&#44; as determined by the element&#39;s author&#44; may be specified on an <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;autonomous&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;3"></a>[autonomous custom element](#autonomous-custom-element)&#44; so long as the attribute name is a <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;valid&#45;attribute&#45;local&#45;name"></a>[valid attribute local name](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-attribute-local-name) and contains no <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;uppercase&#45;ascii&#45;letters"></a>[ASCII upper alphas](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-upper-alpha)&#46; The exception is the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;attr&#45;is&#45;3"></a><code>[is](#attr-is)</code> attribute&#44; which must not be specified on an <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;autonomous&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;4"></a>[autonomous custom element](#autonomous-custom-element) &#40;and which will have no effect if it is&#41;&#46;

<a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;customized&#45;built&#45;in&#45;element&#45;2"></a>[Customized built&#45;in elements](#customized-built-in-element) follow the normal requirements for attributes&#44; based on the elements they extend&#46; To add custom attribute&#45;based behavior&#44; use <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;attr&#45;data&#45;&#42;"></a><code>[data&#45;&#42;](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#attr-data-*)</code> attributes&#46;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

An <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;autonomous&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;5"></a>[autonomous custom element](#autonomous-custom-element) is called a <a id="form&#45;associated&#45;custom&#45;element"></a><strong>form&#45;associated custom element</strong> if the element is associated with a <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;custom&#45;element&#45;definition"></a>[custom element definition](#custom-element-definition) whose <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;concept&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;definition&#45;form&#45;associated"></a>[form&#45;associated](#concept-custom-element-definition-form-associated) field is set to true&#46;

The <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;name&#45;2"></a><code>[name](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#attr-fe-name)</code> attribute represents the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;7"></a>[form&#45;associated custom element](#form-associated-custom-element)&#39;s name&#46; The <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;attr&#45;fe&#45;disabled&#45;2"></a><code>[disabled](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#attr-fe-disabled)</code> attribute is used to make the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;8"></a>[form&#45;associated custom element](#form-associated-custom-element) non&#45;interactive and to prevent its <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;face&#45;submission&#45;value"></a>[submission value](#face-submission-value) from being submitted&#46; The <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;attr&#45;fae&#45;form&#45;2"></a><code>[form](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#attr-fae-form)</code> attribute is used to explicitly associate the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;9"></a>[form&#45;associated custom element](#form-associated-custom-element) with its <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;form&#45;owner"></a>[form owner](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#form-owner)&#46;

The <a id="attr&#45;face&#45;readonly"></a><strong><code>readonly</code></strong> attribute of <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;10"></a>[form&#45;associated custom elements](#form-associated-custom-element) specifies that the element is <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;barred&#45;from&#45;constraint&#45;validation"></a>[barred from constraint validation](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#barred-from-constraint-validation)&#46; User agents don&#39;t provide any other behavior for the attribute&#44; but custom element authors should&#44; where possible&#44; use its presence to make their control non&#45;editable in some appropriate fashion&#44; similar to the behavior for the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;attr&#45;input&#45;readonly"></a>[readonly](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#attr-input-readonly) attribute on built&#45;in form controls&#46;

<strong>Constraint validation</strong>&#58; If the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;attr&#45;face&#45;readonly&#45;2"></a><code>[readonly](#attr-face-readonly)</code> attribute is specified on a <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;11"></a>[form&#45;associated custom element](#form-associated-custom-element)&#44; the element is <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;barred&#45;from&#45;constraint&#45;validation&#45;2"></a>[barred from constraint validation](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#barred-from-constraint-validation)&#46;

The <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;concept&#45;form&#45;reset&#45;control"></a>[reset algorithm](html-language-forms-tables-templates--877d6146487f--2dfc6f632608.md#concept-form-reset-control) for <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;12"></a>[form&#45;associated custom elements](#form-associated-custom-element) is to <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;enqueue&#45;a&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;callback&#45;reaction"></a>[enqueue a custom element callback reaction](#enqueue-a-custom-element-callback-reaction) with the element&#44; callback name &#34;<code>formResetCallback</code>&#34;&#44; and « »&#46;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

A string <var>name</var> is a <a id="valid&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;name"></a><strong>valid custom element name</strong> if all of the following are true&#58;

- <var>name</var> is a <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;valid&#45;element&#45;local&#45;name"></a>[valid element local name](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#valid-element-local-name)&#59;

  <strong>Note&#58;</strong>

  This ensures the custom element can be created with <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;dom&#45;document&#45;createelement"></a><code>[createElement&#40;&#41;](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-document-createelement)</code>&#46;

- <var>name</var>&#39;s 0th <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;code&#45;point"></a>[code point](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#code-point) is an <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;lowercase&#45;ascii&#45;letters"></a>[ASCII lower alpha](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-lower-alpha)&#59;

  <strong>Note&#58;</strong>

  This ensures the HTML parser will treat the name as a tag name instead of as text&#46;

- <var>name</var> does not contain any <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;uppercase&#45;ascii&#45;letters&#45;2"></a>[ASCII upper alphas](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#ascii-upper-alpha)&#59;

  <strong>Note&#58;</strong>

  This ensures the user agent can always treat HTML elements ASCII&#45;case&#45;insensitively&#46;

- <var>name</var> contains a U&#43;002D &#40;&#45;&#41;&#59; and

  <strong>Note&#58;</strong>

  This is used for namespacing and to ensure forward compatibility &#40;since no elements will be added to HTML&#44; SVG&#44; or MathML with hyphen&#45;containing local names going forward&#41;&#46;

- <var>name</var> is not one of the following&#58;

  - &#34;<code>annotation&#45;xml</code>&#34;
  - &#34;<code>color&#45;profile</code>&#34;
  - &#34;<code>font&#45;face</code>&#34;
  - &#34;<code>font&#45;face&#45;src</code>&#34;
  - &#34;<code>font&#45;face&#45;uri</code>&#34;
  - &#34;<code>font&#45;face&#45;format</code>&#34;
  - &#34;<code>font&#45;face&#45;name</code>&#34;
  - &#34;<code>missing&#45;glyph</code>&#34;

  <strong>Note&#58;</strong>

  The list of names above is the summary of all hyphen&#45;containing element names from the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;other&#45;applicable&#45;specifications"></a>[applicable specifications](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#other-applicable-specifications)&#44; namely SVG 2 and MathML&#46; [&#91;SVG&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsSVG) [&#91;MATHML&#93;](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/commit-snapshots/877d6146487f15b15bc8dd0e3c625063a37b456a/#refsMATHML)

Apart from these restrictions&#44; a large variety of names is allowed&#44; to give maximum flexibility for use cases like <code>&#60;math&#45;α&#62;</code> or <code>&#60;emotion&#45;😍&#62;</code>&#46;

------------------------------------------------------------------------

A <a id="custom&#45;element&#45;definition"></a><strong>custom element definition</strong> describes a <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;custom&#45;element&#45;3"></a>[custom element](#custom-element) and consists of&#58;

<strong>A <a id="concept&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;definition&#45;name"></a><strong>name</strong></strong>

A <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;valid&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;name&#45;2"></a>[valid custom element name](#valid-custom-element-name)

<strong>A <a id="concept&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;definition&#45;local&#45;name"></a><strong>local name</strong></strong>

A local name

<strong>A <a id="concept&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;definition&#45;constructor"></a><strong>constructor</strong></strong>

A Web IDL <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;customelementconstructor"></a><code>[CustomElementConstructor](#customelementconstructor)</code> callback function type value wrapping the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;custom&#45;element&#45;constructor"></a>[custom element constructor](#custom-element-constructor)

<strong>A list of <a id="concept&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;definition&#45;observed&#45;attributes"></a><strong>observed attributes</strong></strong>

A <code>sequence&#60;DOMString&#62;</code>

<strong>A collection of <a id="concept&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;definition&#45;lifecycle&#45;callbacks"></a><strong>lifecycle callbacks</strong></strong>

A map&#44; whose keys are the strings &#34;<code>connectedCallback</code>&#34;&#44; &#34;<code>disconnectedCallback</code>&#34;&#44; &#34;<code>connectedMoveCallback</code>&#34;&#44; &#34;<code>adoptedCallback</code>&#34;&#44; &#34;<code>attributeChangedCallback</code>&#34;&#44; &#34;<code>formAssociatedCallback</code>&#34;&#44; &#34;<code>formDisabledCallback</code>&#34;&#44; &#34;<code>formResetCallback</code>&#34;&#44; and &#34;<code>formStateRestoreCallback</code>&#34;&#46; The corresponding values are either a Web IDL <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;idl&#45;function"></a><code>[Function](https://webidl.spec.whatwg.org/#common-Function)</code> callback function type value&#44; or null&#46; By default the value of each entry is null&#46;

<strong>A <a id="concept&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;definition&#45;construction&#45;stack"></a><strong>construction stack</strong></strong>

A list&#44; initially empty&#44; that is manipulated by the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;concept&#45;upgrade&#45;an&#45;element"></a>[upgrade an element](#concept-upgrade-an-element) algorithm and the [HTML element constructors](html-language-foundations--877d6146487f--b55e73c31978.md#html-element-constructors)&#46; Each entry in the list will be either an element or an <a id="concept&#45;already&#45;constructed&#45;marker"></a><strong><em>already constructed</em> marker</strong>&#46;

<strong>A <a id="concept&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;definition&#45;form&#45;associated"></a><strong>form&#45;associated</strong> boolean</strong>

If this is true&#44; user agent treats elements associated to this <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;custom&#45;element&#45;definition&#45;2"></a>[custom element definition](#custom-element-definition) as <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;form&#45;associated&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;13"></a>[form&#45;associated custom elements](#form-associated-custom-element)&#46;

<strong>A <a id="concept&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;definition&#45;disable&#45;internals"></a><strong>disable internals</strong> boolean</strong>

Controls <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;dom&#45;attachinternals"></a><code>[attachInternals&#40;&#41;](#dom-attachinternals)</code>&#46;

<strong>A <a id="concept&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;definition&#45;disable&#45;shadow"></a><strong>disable shadow</strong> boolean</strong>

Controls <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;dom&#45;element&#45;attachshadow"></a><code>[attachShadow&#40;&#41;](https://dom.spec.whatwg.org/#dom-element-attachshadow)</code>&#46;

To <a id="look&#45;up&#45;a&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;definition"></a><strong>look up a custom element definition</strong>&#44; given null or a <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;customelementregistry"></a><code>[CustomElementRegistry](#customelementregistry)</code> object <var>registry</var>&#44; string&#45;or&#45;null <var>namespace</var>&#44; string <var>localName</var>&#44; and string&#45;or&#45;null <var>is</var>&#44; perform the following steps&#46; They will return either a <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;custom&#45;element&#45;definition&#45;3"></a>[custom element definition](#custom-element-definition) or null&#58;

1.  If <var>registry</var> is null&#44; then return null&#46;

2.  If <var>namespace</var> is not the <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;html&#45;namespace&#45;2"></a>[HTML namespace](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#html-namespace)&#44; then return null&#46;

3.  If <var>registry</var>&#39;s <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;custom&#45;element&#45;definition&#45;set"></a>[custom element definition set](#custom-element-definition-set) <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;list&#45;contains"></a>[contains](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-contain) an item with <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;concept&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;definition&#45;name&#45;3"></a>[name](#concept-custom-element-definition-name) and <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;concept&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;definition&#45;local&#45;name"></a>[local name](#concept-custom-element-definition-local-name) both equal to <var>localName</var>&#44; then return that item&#46;

4.  If <var>registry</var>&#39;s <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;custom&#45;element&#45;definition&#45;set&#45;2"></a>[custom element definition set](#custom-element-definition-set) <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;list&#45;contains&#45;2"></a>[contains](https://infra.spec.whatwg.org/#list-contain) an item with <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;concept&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;definition&#45;name&#45;4"></a>[name](#concept-custom-element-definition-name) equal to <var>is</var> and <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;core&#45;concepts&#58;concept&#45;custom&#45;element&#45;definition&#45;local&#45;name&#45;2"></a>[local name](#concept-custom-element-definition-local-name) equal to <var>localName</var>&#44; then return that item&#46;

5.  Return null&#46;

#### <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;api"></a>4&#46;13&#46;4 The <a id="custom&#45;elements&#45;api&#58;customelementregistry"></a><code>[CustomElementRegistry](#customelementregistry)</code> interface[](#custom-elements-api)
